children.translated_text: Obeisance to <s>Śrī Gaṇeśa</s>.
Beginning of the <s>Bhāratī Bhūṣaṇa</s> (Ornament of Speech).
<s>Dohā</s> (couplet):
Through <s>Vallabha</s>'s ocean of compassion, all afflictions are removed. (1) She who is the boat for crossing the ocean of worldly existence (<s>bhava</s>),
I bow to her, in whose pride there is no cruelty.
I constantly bow to the lotus feet of <s>Hari</s>, placed in the heart. (2) The enchanting one, the mind's honored one — always meditating on Speech (<s>Vāṇī</s>),
describing the ornaments [of speech], the wise <s>Giridharadāsa</s> [composes this]. (3)
Adorned with beautiful descriptions and poetic qualities, this is the <s>Bhāratī Bhūṣaṇa</s> (Ornament of Speech).
Read it, praise it, learn it, hear it — together with the love of true poets. (4) Definition of <s>Upamā</s> (Simile):
That is <s>Upamā</s> (simile) where, in describing, <s>upameya</s> (the subject of comparison) and <s>upamāna</s> (the standard of comparison)
are always adorned with equality — thus the wise poets declare. (5) Example:
The face [is like] the moon, the forehead mark [like] that of a lion, the waist graceful [like] a lion's;
the beautiful <s>Rādhikā</s> was filled with an abundance of delight. (6) Definition of <s>Upamāna</s> etc.:
That to which similarity is attributed is called the <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison);
that which is described as equal is the <s>upameya</s> (subject of comparison), nothing else. (7) The quality
perceived as common to both <s>upameya</s> and <s>upamāna</s> — that is the <s>sādhāraṇa dharma</s> (common property); thus describe, O poet-king.
(8) The word that conveys equality is named the <s>upamā vācaka</s> (simile-indicator).
<s>Giridharadāsa</s> describes thus the definition, clear and delightful. (9) Conch, lotus, and
<s>bimba</s> fruit, parrot, gold, oyster-shell — these and others are <s>upamānas</s> (standards of comparison);
understand them, O lamp of the poet-clan. (10) Throat, eyes, braid of hair, lips,
nose, ears — these and others are the <s>upameyas</s> (subjects of comparison); the wise of noble intellect describe them
in silence. (11) Beauty, delicacy, darkness, charm —
these are the <s>sādhāraṇa dharmas</s> (common properties), the heart-stealing abode of aesthetic delight (<s>rasa</s>). (12) 'Like' (<s>lauṃ</s>), 'as' (<s>so</s>), 'similar' (<s>sī</s>),
'resembling' (<s>sarisa</s>), 'equal' (<s>sama</s>), 'same' (<s>samāna</s>), 'like' (<s>iva</s>), 'comparable' (<s>tūla</s>) —

'such as' (<s>aiso</s>), 'of this kind' (<s>aise</s>), 'this sort' — these are the roots of <s>upamā vācaka</s> (simile-indicators). (13) 'As' (<s>jimi</s>), 'thus' (<s>timi</s>), 'just as' (<s>jaiso</s>), 'exactly so' (<s>itaiso</s>), 'as' (<s>yathā</s>), 'so' (<s>tathā</s>), 'in which manner' (<s>jyoṃ</s>),
'in that manner' (<s>tyoṃ</s>) — these too are <s>upamā vācakas</s>; when two are combined, they become [a pair]. (14)
Definition of <s>Pūrṇopamā</s> (Complete Simile): Where <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s>, along with the <s>upamā vācaka</s>,
together with the <s>sādhāraṇa dharma</s> — that is <s>Pūrṇopamā</s> (Complete Simile). (15) Example:
Night-joy-giving, like the full moon, with <s>śapharī</s>-fish-like moving eyes;
slender of waist like <s>Hari</s>'s <s>Laṅkā</s>, standing exactly mirror-like. (16) <s>Luptopamā</s> (Elliptical Simile):
When among the four [components] — <s>upamāna</s> etc. — one, two, or three are omitted,
consider it <s>Luptopamā</s> (Elliptical Simile). (17) The first is <s>vācaka-luptā</s> — a simile without the indicator word;
the second is called <s>dharma-luptā</s> — one devoid of the common property. (18)
The third is <s>vācaka-dharma-luptā</s>, O excellent wise poet — without indicator
and without the <s>upameya</s>, the fourth is the delightful one. (19) The fifth is without <s>upamāna</s>, without indicator and <s>upamāna</s>.
The sixth is without dharma and <s>upamāna</s>; know the seventh as <s>luptā</s>. (20) <s>Upamāna</s>, indicator, and dharma omitted — know the eighth.
Eight types of <s>Luptopamā</s> — poet-folk declare and explain. (21) Example of <s>vācaka-luptā</s>:
[Missing indicator word in the simile.]
The face a full moon, beautiful; pure lotus-petal eyes;
golden-vine-like graceful body; butter-sweet words. (22) Example of <s>dharma-luptā</s>:
Lightning-vine-like the city-woman, dark like a rain-cloud full of water;
in the beautiful grove, both exceedingly charming. (23) Example of <s>vācaka-dharma-luptā</s>:
Words of nectar, eyes of <s>Madana</s>'s (Cupid's) arrows, armies upon armies;
the face [like] the night-lord (moon) — behold <s>Hari</s>'s night of delight, the excellent night. (24) Example of <s>vācaka-upameya-luptā</s>:
The balcony rose — as if the full moon had taken form and beauty.
Come, devoted one, come and behold <s>Manmatha</s>'s (Cupid's) hands of bliss. (25) Example of <s>upamāna-luptā</s>:
Beautiful throat, dove-like; <s>Kehari</s>-like slender waist;
whose <s>Hari</s>-like sparkling speech — O <s>Hari</s>, absorbed in the grove. (26) <s>Vācaka-upamāna-luptopamā</s>:
The lamp of the house, the beloved shines, garland of serpents adorning the neck;
for what reason does <s>Hari</s> remain silent? Ask, and give the answer. (27) Example of <s>dharma-upamāna-luptā</s>:
Cloud-colored, thundering, roaming, dealing death-like destruction;
ocean-like in depth — <s>Tripurāri</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), steady in battle. (28) Example of <s>upamāna-vācaka-dharma-luptā</s>:
Deer-eyed, elephant-gaited, cuckoo-voiced, delicate lady;
<s>Kehari</s>-like waist, beautiful — behold the woman, O <s>Murāri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>). (29) <s>Mālopamā</s> (Garland Simile):
Where for a single <s>upameya</s>, many <s>upamānas</s> are used in description —
that is called <s>Mālopamā</s> by the wise, discerning poets. (30) Example:
Like a deer's [eyes], like <s>Manmatha</s>'s (Cupid's) arrows, deep like a fish, pure;
like <s>kañjana</s> (collyrium), like a <s>khañjana</s> (wagtail bird), mind-delighting, so beautiful. (31) Definition of <s>Rasanopamā</s> (Chain Simile):
Where the first-stated <s>upameya</s> becomes the <s>upamāna</s> [for the next] —
that is called <s>Rasanopamā</s> by those who are chief among the world's good poets. (32) Example:
Wisdom like devotion, devotion like humility, humility like grace, grace like beautiful <s>Rati</s>;
<s>Rati</s> like movement, movement like devotion — then I am the son of the Wind (<s>Hanumān</s>). (33) Definition of <s>Anvaya</s>:
Where one thing has both <s>upameya</s>-ness and <s>upamāna</s>-ness,
and there is no equality with another — that is <s>Anvaya</s>. (34) Example:
Your fame is purer than your fame; your fame is [also] dark.
Like the celestial river (<s>Gaṅgā</s>), the celestial river — full of beauty and delight. (35) Definition of <s>Upameyopamā</s> (Mutual Simile):
Where two things are mutually both <s>upameya</s> and <s>upamāna</s>,
that is <s>Upameyopamā</s>; the third element is the equality. (36) Example:
Pure lotus-like are the eyes; the lotus is pure like the eyes.
Beautiful, dark like <s>Kāma</s> (Cupid); <s>Hari</s> is equal to <s>Kāma</s> in appearance. (37) Definition of <s>Pratīpa</s> (Reversed Comparison):
When the <s>upameya</s> is made the <s>upamāna</s> — says <s>Giridharadāsa</s> —
among the five [types of] <s>Pratīpa</s>, know the first as the chief. (38) Example:
Then, like your body, is <s>Kāma</s>'s; then like your face are these tresses;
new shoots are [like] your lips; the conch-throat matches. (39) Definition of the second <s>Pratīpa</s>:
Where the <s>upameya</s> removes the pride of the <s>upamāna</s>,
those of immeasurable intellect call that the second <s>Pratīpa</s>. (40) Example:
Why does one's own beauty boast ignorantly?

<s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), <s>Umā</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>), <s>Śacī</s> (<s>Indra</s>'s wife), <s>Śāradā</s> (<s>Sarasvatī</s>) — you are like these and more. (41) Definition of the third <s>Pratīpa</s>:
When the <s>upamāna</s> receives disrespect from the <s>upameya</s>,
the wise poets, protectors of the earth, call that the third <s>Pratīpa</s>. (42) Example:
Why do you boast of lowliness, O <s>Urvīca</s> (one of the earth)?
More than an outcaste in the world is the <s>Hari</s>-hater. (43) Definition of the fourth <s>Pratīpa</s>:
When the <s>upamāna</s> is manifestly not worthy of being equated,
<s>Giridharadāsa</s> [says] that <s>Pratīpa</s> is the fourth, O discerning one. (44) Example:
Your face is such — O son of the lotus-pond — and this companion: this matter
is described in vain; the apprehensive poet's intellect is the poor man's explanation. (45) Definition of the fifth <s>Pratīpa</s>:
When the <s>upamāna</s> becomes useless near the superior <s>upameya</s>,
<s>Giridharadāsa</s> explains — that is the fifth <s>Pratīpa</s>. (46) Example:
Seeing the beautiful woman — what is <s>Urvaśī</s>?
What are <s>Mainā</s>, <s>Maina</s>, the heavenly woman, <s>Kamalā</s>, or <s>Śailakumārī</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>)? (47) Definition of <s>Rūpaka</s> (Metaphor), two types:

children.translated_text: When a subject is described with the subject [itself], making identity (<s>abheda</s>) in its own form —
with exaggeration, diminution, or equality — that is the six-fold form of <s>Rūpaka</s> (Metaphor). (48) Example of <s>adhikokti-abheda-rūpaka</s> (exaggerated identity-metaphor):
Mounted on the elephant of wealth, riding through the sky, the enemy of <s>Indra</s> beholds;
nectar-dripping moon-umbrella on the head — pearls scattered, the world glittering. (49) Example of <s>nyūnokti-rūpaka</s> (diminished metaphor):
The flower-bow (<s>Kāma</s>'s bow) without flowers — behold it absorbed in the grove;
gone through the world, this pure <s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) — a lotus without a lotus. (50) Example of <s>samokti-abheda-rūpaka</s> (equal identity-metaphor):
Your face-moon, remover of sorrow, abode of nectar-showering beauty,
delighting the night, beloved of the <s>rasika</s> (connoisseur), removing darkness, giving bliss. (51) Example of <s>adhikokti-tadrūpa-rūpaka</s> (exaggerated same-form metaphor):
The fame-dust, the virtue-dust — exceeding that, the three worlds tremble;
<s>Dharmamitra</s>, the great friend — dying and living in companionship. (52) Example of <s>nyūnokti-tadrūpa-rūpaka</s> (diminished same-form metaphor):
The wealth-lord (<s>Kubera</s>), the people's lord — this is not [one] seated on the <s>Puṣpaka</s> [chariot];
a second <s>Gaṇeśa</s>, beautifully dressed, pure — shining, but without a trunk. (53) Example of <s>samokti-tadrūpa-rūpaka</s> (equal same-form metaphor):
This one sustains the world; that one destroys the other's side;
the other one, of enchanting form — lotus-pure, exactly matching. (54) Definition of <s>Pariṇāma</s> (Transformation):
When two described <s>upamānas</s> perform some action —
<s>Giridharadāsa</s> explains — its name is <s>Pariṇāma</s>. (55) Example:
From the lotus-feet he walks gracefully; with the lotus-hand he takes the grove;
from the lotus-face <s>Hari</s> speaks words, composing delightful utterances. (56) Definition of <s>Ullekha</s> (Description):
When one thing is perceived by many in many ways — describing one in many manners —
both [types of] <s>Ullekha</s> ornament, the excellent poets describe with delight. (57) Example of the first <s>Ullekha</s>:
The women [see him as] <s>Kāma</s> (Cupid); the <s>Yādavas</s> [as] their benefactor; [as] <s>Nanda</s>'s son, of fresh limbs.
<s>Kaṃsa</s> sees <s>Yama</s> (Death); the sages see <s>Hari</s>; the enchanting one enters the stage. (58) Example of the second <s>Ullekha</s>:
In radiance, the sun; in joy-giving, the moon; to enemies, Death (<s>Kāla</s>), the delightful one;

to the women of <s>Vraja</s>, <s>Kāma</s> (Cupid) — ah, always the dark, wealthy one (<s>Śyāma</s>). (59) Definition of <s>Smaraṇa</s> (Recollection), <s>Bhrama</s> (Confusion), <s>Sandeha</s> (Doubt):
<s>Smaraṇa</s>, <s>Bhrama</s>, and <s>Sandeha</s> — these are three ornaments (<s>alaṅkāras</s>);
the accomplished wise poets describe them by their definitions and names. (60) Example of <s>Smaraṇa</s> (Recollection):
Hearing the cuckoo's melody, the memory of [her] words comes to the mindful one;
seeing the moon-face, the memory arises — the body's awareness is like the cloud's splendor. (61) Example of <s>Bhrama</s> (Confusion):
Mistaking the dark-cloud-colored [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] for a rain-cloud, the forest peacocks rose and danced;
mistaking you for a golden wand, thieves roam in every direction. (62) Example of <s>Sandeha</s> (Doubt):
Is she <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) or <s>Rādhā</s>? Is it the speech of <s>Girijā</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>)? Know it as <s>Rati</s>'s [speech].
Is he the dark <s>Kāma</s> (Cupid) or the wish-fulfilling tree (<s>Kalpataru</s>)? <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the joy-giver. (63) Definition of <s>Śuddhāpahṇuti</s> (Pure Concealment):
When a [common] property is concealed and something else is superimposed, O wise one —
the discerning poets call that <s>Śuddhāpahṇuti</s>, an ornament (<s>alaṅkāra</s>). (64) Example:
The dark one (<s>Śyāma</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) did not wear a yellow garment — [it is] the play of lightning in the cloud;
that is not a garland on [his] head — [it is] the crescent moon's radiance. (65) Definition of <s>Hetvapahṇuti</s> (Concealment with Reason):
That same <s>Śuddhāpahṇuti</s>, where there is reasoning and logic —
<s>Giridharadāsa</s> explains — that is <s>Hetvapahṇuti</s> (Concealment with Reason). (66) Example:
The women do not walk in the dark night and grove — the golden vine cannot go;
breaking free from the cloud, many clouds [appear] — lightning appears. (67) Definition of <s>Paryastāpahṇuti</s> (Reversed Concealment):
When the qualities of one subject are superimposed upon another —
then the poets call it <s>Paryastāpahṇuti</s>, truly. (68) Example:
This is not <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>), the lord of gods — the lord of gods is <s>Nandakumāra</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>);
this is not the jewel-mine ocean — this is the marketplace of <s>Mathurā</s> city. (69) Definition of <s>Hetu-paryastāpahṇuti</s> (Reversed Concealment with Reason):
A <s>Paryastāpahṇuti</s> that includes a reason —
that conceals a property with reasoning — that becomes its name. (70) Example:
The darkness-remover is not the sun — it is the worship of <s>Hari</s>; [if] darkness remains, the sun is seen [to be insufficient].
Wherever darkness remains and <s>Hari</s> is not worshipped — thus describe, O wise one. (71) Definition of <s>Bhrāntāpahṇuti</s> (Confused Concealment):
When through confusion, one thing is mistakenly called another through words —
the poet-folk, [like] <s>Giridharadāsa</s>, call that <s>Bhrāntāpahṇuti</s>. (72) Example:
The dark cloud (<s>Śyāma-ghana</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) gave life; the beloved night has come.
Why, O friend, without the rainy season — no, no, the king of <s>Gokula</s> [has come]. (73) Definition of <s>Chekāpahṇuti</s> (Clever Concealment):
When one destroys another's doubt and conceals the true matter — the poets call that <s>Chekāpahṇuti</s>,
[...way. 74.] Example: Having drawn the bark-garment to cover the body, before <s>Hari</s>'s adorn-
-ment. 'Why in the bowers, O friend? <s>Śyāma</s> (Krishna) [is] not [there] — [it is merely] a <s>karīla</s> tre-'
'-e.' 75. Definition of <s>Kaitavāpahnuti</s> (Deceptive Denial): When one thing is described as anoth-
-er, making a false identification — the wise call that the ornament of <s>kaitavāpahnuti</s> (deceptive denial),
[say] the discerning. 76. Example: In the guise of breasts, <s>Manmatha</s> (Cupid) churns,
dwelling in the woman's bosom. In the guise of the monsoon, with lightning <s>Indra</s> creates
terror there. 77. Definition of <s>Utprekṣā</s> (Poetic Fancy): There are three kinds of <s>utprekṣā</s> — thus
say the learned: by <s>vastu</s> (object), <s>hetu</s> (cause), and <s>phala</s> (result) — those whose intellect
is rich in aesthetic taste. 78. Description of the divisions of object, cause, and result: The object-fancy is of two kinds — explicit-basis
and implicit-basis, know this. Cause and result [each have] the established-basis and the un-
established-basis, understand this. 79. Example of <s>Uktāspadavastūtprekṣā</s> (Explicit-basis Object-fancy): The
<s>hālāhala</s> (deadly poison) pours forth greatly, a net of <s>Bhārata</s>-war flames. As if churning the ocean,
as if drawing forth the flame of the submarine fire (<s>baḍavānala</s>). 80. Example of <s>Anuktāspadavastūtprekṣā</s> (Implicit-basis
Object-fancy): The moon rains down, as if shooting arrows of golden rays.
In <s>Sāvana</s> (the monsoon month), the clouds begin to race, moving unevenly like the host of <s>Yama</s>. 81. Established-basis
Cause-fancy Example (<s>Hetusiddhāspadotprekṣā</s>): These [cheeks] shine by your hands, as if having grasped the ro-
-pe of the swing — the reflected shadow falls, as if [making] the young <s>Nandakiśora</s> (Krishna) dark. 82.
Example of <s>Hetuasiddhāspadotprekṣā</s> (Unestablished-basis Cause-fancy): Those eyes desire equality, as if
they were sharp arrows — released from the king's pride, they take the life of the deer.
83. Example of <s>Phalasiddhāspadotprekṣā</s> (Established-basis Result-fancy): Seeing me, the lightning
shrank back and entered the clouds again — just so the virtuous woman, as if closing her
face, came and sat in the chamber. 84. Example of <s>Phalāsiddhāspadotprekṣā</s> (Unestablished-basis Result-fancy):
For the sake of equaling your waist, as if the lion dwells in the forest. For equaling your breasts,
as if the mountains endure snow, sunshine, and wind. 85. The Indicator of <s>Utprekṣā</s> (Poetic Fancy):
The indicators of <s>utprekṣā</s> are words such as 'as if' (<s>manhu</s>), 'as though' (<s>manu</s>), 'as it were' (<s>janu</s>), and the like. Where [these are] not [present],
know that to be <s>gamyotprekṣā</s> (implied fancy). 86. Example of <s>Gamyotprekṣā</s> (Implied Fancy):
On your bank, the flowers of the trees, abodes of finest fragrance — the <s>Yamunā</s> is worship-
-ping the sacred site of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>. 87. Definition of <s>Rūpakātiśayokti</s> (Metaphorical Hyperbole):
Where, omitting the indicator and the object of comparison (<s>upameya</s>), only the standard of comparison (<s>upamāna</s>) is stated — <s>rūpakātiśaya</s>-
<s>ukti</s> — thus describe it, O treasury of wisdom. 88. Example: In the moon, the poi-
-son of trees appears as a <s>kunda</s>-garland. On the heat [appears] a parrot, on the parrot a bow, with
diverse aesthetic essence perceived. 89. Definition of <s>Sāpahnavarūpakātiśayokti</s> (Denial-Metaphor Hyperbole):
Where the reversed denial (<s>paryastāpahnuti</s>) is combined with proper ornamentation — there is the <s>sāpahnava-rūpaka</s>
(denial-metaphor) combined with <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole). 90. Example: In your face
dwells nectar (<s>sudhā</s>), O tender <s>Rādhā</s>! That is what they call the moon — without
understanding, the deluded one. 91. Definition of <s>Bhedakātiśayokti</s> (Differentiating Hyperbole): The separate words
[that] differentiate where there is <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) — <s>bhedakātiśayokti</s>, the fine
ornament, is that. 92. Example: Her glances are different, her speech is
different, her laughter and swaying are each something else. Her coming, her soft singing — all are something
else — these are her ways. 93. Definition of <s>Sambandhātiśayokti</s> (Relational Hyperbole): Where a relati-
-onship through poetic art makes the unconnected appear connected — <s>sambandhātiśayokti</s>, thus
describe the learned. 94. Example: Departing from the city of <s>Avadha</s> (Ayodhyā),
he drinks the water, filling his trunk from the celestial river. Taking a pitcher from <s>Dhruva</s>'s abode,
your <s>Rāma</s>'s elephant. 95. Definition of <s>Asambandhātiśayokti</s> (Unrelated Hyperbole): That which
makes what is unconnected appear connected when the intellect illuminates according to understanding — <s>asambandha</s>-
<s>atiśayokti</s> (unrelated hyperbole), says <s>Giridhara Dāsa</s>. 96. Example:
How does the sun gain its honor? By seeing your radiance, O king! The poet enters
[into the understanding that the sun is] always dishonored in form [compared to you]. 97. Definition of <s>Akramātiśayokti</s> (Disordered Hyperbole):
When both cause and effect are described simultaneously — <s>akramātiśaya</s>-
<s>ukti</s> — that ornament is a limb of poetry. 98. Example: He arose, and at once
an elephant in hand, a lotus, a discus in the hand of the discus-bearer (<s>Cakradhara</s>, Viṣṇu). From the hand the discus on the crocodile's head clea-
-ves and strikes at once. 99. Definition of <s>Capalātiśayokti</s> (Swift Hyperbole): The cause
— merely upon hearing its name, the effect instantly occurs — <s>capalātiśaya</s>-
<s>ukti</s>, this is that ornament. 100. Example: As soon as one said 'Go to another land,'
O beloved, hearing this the girl wasted away. The ring reached her hand, and [it]
reached the garland at her neck. 101. Definition of <s>Atyantātiśayokti</s> (Extreme Hyperbole): The sequence of before and after
does not correspond — that, says <s>Giridhara Dāsa</s>, is <s>atyantātiśayokti</s> (extreme hyperbole).
The poets illuminate [this]. 102. Example: <s>Hanumān</s>'s tai-
-l had not yet caught fire, [yet] all of <s>Laṅkā</s> was already burned, and the <s>Rākṣasas</s> (night-
-stalkers) had fled. 103. Definition of <s>Tulyayogitā</s> (Equal Conjunction): When an action or quality
possesses a common property — for the described and for the other — [that is] <s>tulyayogi</s>-
<s>tā</s>, that [is it]. 104. Example of <s>Prastutatulyayogitā</s> (Contextual Equal Conjunction): The dawn ri-
-ses — seeing it, the <s>kuvalaya</s> (blue lotus) shrinks and thieves [shrink]. Seeing the moonrise, the fair
lady's face and the lotus [bloom] in all directions. 105. Example of <s>Aprastutatulyayogitā</s>
(Non-contextual Equal Conjunction): Seeing your tenderness, O woman, in this world — the lo-
-tus and the rose — no one calls them hard. 106. Definition of the second <s>Tulyayogitā</s>:
When equal activity in the beneficial and the harmful is described, without
interruption — this is the other <s>tulyayogitā</s>, thus describe the thoughtful poets
— 107. Example: <s>Giridhara Dāsa</s> [says], in the world, you are exceed-
-ingly clever, O wise one. Playing in the lake, you steal the pride of both women and enemies.
108. Definition of the third <s>Tulyayogitā</s>: When one makes equal the superior qualities
of many to one alone — that is the third <s>tulyayogitā</s>, say
the king of poets. 109. Example: You [are like] <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Budha</s> (Mercury), the Moon, the lord of the gods
(<s>Indra</s>), <s>Śiva</s> (bearer of the moon), [and] a treasury of wisdom. You, O king, are a <s>kalpataru</s> (wish-fulfilling tree), a treasure
of virtues, clever and wise. 110. Definition of <s>Dīpaka</s> (Illuminator): Where the non-described and
the described share a single common quality — the ornament named <s>dīpaka</s> (illuminator)
— thus should it be stated. 111. Example: The king shines day by day with
gardens blooming with fruits and flowers, with tall bodies the excellent elephants, with [fine] gait the horses,
always. 112. Definition of <s>Āvṛttadīpaka</s> (Repeated Illuminator): The repeated <s>dīpaka</s> has three kinds
— the word-repeated, know as one; the meaning-repeated, and the word-and-meaning
repeated — recognize them thus. 113. Example of <s>Padāvṛttidīpaka</s> (Word-repeated Illuminator):
<s>Nanda</s>'s son (Krishna) makes love, great affection grows. Touching the beau-
-tiful, passionate woman — touching with the corners of the eyes meeting. 114. Example of <s>Arthāvṛttidīpaka</s> (Meaning-repeated
Illuminator): The war-maddened elephants charge, the host of horses runs,
the actors perform on stage, many actresses dance, the actors rejoice. 115. Example of <s>Padārthāvṛtti-</s>
<s>dīpaka</s> (Word-and-Meaning-repeated Illuminator): In battle, <s>Rāma</s> roars, the ten-
-headed one (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>) roars. Filled with rage, the night-stalkers (<s>Rākṣasas</s>) rush in both directions, rushing the
monkeys (<s>kīśa</s>). 116. Definition of <s>Prativastūpamā</s> (Counter-simile): When objects of equal
standing — the compared (<s>upameya</s>) and the standard (<s>upamāna</s>) — are stated in separate phrases, <s>prativastūpa</s>-
<s>mā</s> (counter-simile), know this. 117. Example: Keeping the company of the good, the wicked person's
wickedness does not go away. Even drinking nectar (<s>sudhā</s>), the serpent does not give up its venom, the giver of suffer-
-ing. 118. Definition of <s>Dṛṣṭānta</s> (Illustration): When the described and the non-described, both having distinct
qualities shown — where [they relate] as image and reflection — that is called <s>dṛṣṭānta</s>
(illustration). 119. Example: The beautiful one — that is you; <s>Ratī</s> (goddess of love) and the famous
[beauty] — know this. O king, you are the wise and generous one; accept [this comparison to] a divine <s>surataru</s> (wish-tree). 120.
Definition of <s>Nidarśanā</s> (Exemplification): The poets describe three kinds of <s>nidarśanā</s> with dis-
-cernment: the two similar sentence-meanings, and the superimposition as one. 121.
Example: For the generous one whose heart is simple, there is no appearance of crookedness.
The full moon's spotlessness — know this, says <s>Giridhara Dāsa</s>. 122.
Definition of the second <s>Nidarśanā</s>: When the standard of comparison (<s>upamāna</s>) and the object of comparison (<s>upameya</s>) take on each other's qualities,
reversed — that is the second <s>nidarśanā</s>, says the king of poets. 123.
Example: Taking the restlessness of the fish, behold the woman's eyes! The ki-
-ng's hand has taken its generosity from the beautiful wish-fulfilling tree (<s>surataru</s>). 124. Third
<s>Nidarśanā</s> definition: Where the true meaning and the untrue meaning are made known through the action of understanding —
there is the third <s>nidarśanā</s>, all poets describe. 125. True-
meaning example: Always bearing the water of the <s>guru</s>'s feet upon one's head, just as
<s>Mahādeva</s> (Śiva) bears the <s>Gaṅgā</s> on his head with love. 126. Untrue-meaning
example: Fearlessness against the great — [such a one] goes on announcing [his own] destruction.
Confronting a torch, the lamp-wick is extinguished at once. 127. <s>Vyati</s>-
<s>reka</s> (Contrast) definition: Where a distinction is described in the described and non-described, by the king of poets —
with the divisions of superior, inferior, and equal — that is called <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast). 128.
Example of the superior: O king, more than the <s>kalpataru</s> (wish-tree) are you, in splendor and wisdom especial-
-ly. The woman's lips are more than young leaves — behold, greater in the taste of nectar (<s>amṛta</s>). 129.
Example of the inferior: Compared to <s>Hari</s> (Viṣṇu), the devotee (<s>harijana</s>) is on his knees; <s>Hari</s> rests in every vessel (heart),
[yet] the crooked serpent, like a spy, bites and makes an end [of things]. 130.
Example of the equal: One who falls into his own domain crushes and grinds [the enemy];
but the company of what is wholesome is never grasped by the host of the wicked, ever. 131. <s>Saho</s>-
<s>kti</s> (Co-expression) definition: Where, to delight the mind, many things are described together — that
is the ornament of <s>sahokti</s> (co-expression), renowned in texts. 132. Example:
Cleverness came, bringing youthfulness to your limbs; with <s>Manamohana</s> (Krishna, the mind-enchanter), the heart
merged through these very eyes. 133. Definition of <s>Vinokti</s> (Expression-without): Of two kinds, they say
the <s>vinokti</s>, by the mirror of the good poet's intellect: the contextual [appears] somewhat lesser without [something],
and somewhat without beauty-giving [quality]. 134. Example of the first <s>Vinokti</s>:
Without a poet, the assembly does not shine; without the night, [there is no] abode of nectar (the moon). Not fitting
is <s>Giridhara Dāsa</s> without <s>Giridhara</s> (Krishna/mountain-bearer), [says] <s>Giridhara Dāsa</s>. 135. Second
<s>vinokti</s> example: Blessed, blessed is the wealthy one! Without the city, [his] passing [of time]
[is] pleasant. The kingdom of <s>Rāma</s> — your good fame produces [it]; again <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) manifests. 136.
Definition of <s>Samāsokti</s> (Condensed Expression): When in the contextual, the non-contextual incidents
flash forth — that is the ornament of <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression), says the delight of the poet-clan. 137.
Example: O friend, having found the night, the moon roams about, filled to the brim with aesthetic delight (<s>rasa</s>).
Embracing the eastern horizon, joyful, stretching forth his hands — the sun. 138. <s>Pari</s>-
<s>kara</s> (Circumstance) definition: Where an adjective (<s>viśeṣaṇa</s>) is given along with a delightful intention —
<s>Giridhara Dāsa</s> says, name it as the ornament of <s>parikara</s> (circumstance). 139. Exam-
-ple: Beholding <s>Cakrapāṇi Hari</s> (discus-wielding Viṣṇu), the demon host flees far away.
Raining nectar, dark as a cloud, you remove affliction, full of joy. 140. <s>Pari</s>-
<s>karāṅkura</s> (Germ of Circumstance) definition: Where the qualified (<s>viśeṣya</s>) itself is described with an intention together
with [the qualifier] — that is the ornament of <s>parikarāṅkura</s> (germ of circumstance), a limb of poetry. 141.
Example: Today, O beloved, many words of the peacock-season have been spoken.
The immeasurable glory of the sun comes forth. (142) Definition of <s>Śleṣa</s> (Pun):
<s>Śleṣa</s> (pun) has many meanings — the learned call it an ornament; based on the described
and non-described, it has three kinds. (143) Example of <s>Śleṣa</s> with multiple meanings relating to the subject (<s>Prakṛta</s>):
The serpent-rider (<s>Hari</s>/one who rides the serpent) conquered the enemy's army; he who destroyed the host of hell (<s>Naraka</s>),
endowed with victorious allies and kinsmen of strength — worship <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the one of curved speech. (144)
Example of <s>Śleṣa</s> with multiple meanings relating to the non-subject (<s>Aprakṛta</s>): Those women departed — life-giving, pleasant, and beautiful,
dwelling in the heart of <s>Ghanaśyāma</s> (dark-cloud-hued <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), excellent like the <s>sāraṅga</s> (rain-bird/deer),
most beautiful. (145) Example of <s>Śleṣa</s> with multiple meanings relating to both subject and non-subject (<s>Prakṛtāprakṛta</s>):
<s>Rati</s>'s beloved (<s>Kāma</s>/love), with flower-hands, beautiful, dark-hued and charming in color,
seized the lotuses in the water amidst poison — the one with the fish-banner (<s>Kāmadeva</s>), most generous. (146) Definition of <s>Aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (Praise of the Irrelevant):
When through the description of the irrelevant, the relevant subject is conveyed,
the kings of poets call it <s>Aprastutapraśaṃsā</s>. (157) Example: Blessed is
<s>Śeṣa</s> (the serpent), who for the world's benefit bears the burden of the earth upon his head; wretched is the wicked one who, without offense,
destroys the honor of the <s>cakora</s> bird (one devoted to love). (148) Definition of <s>Prastutāṅkura</s> (Hint of the Relevant):
When the indication of the relevant subject is itself relevant,
everyone calls that ornament <s>Prastutāṅkura</s>. (149) Example: O you who abandon the <s>Gaṅgā</s> (<s>Mandākinī</s>),
bathing in a mere petty stream — why, O bee, forsaking the <s>mālatī</s> jasmine,
do you go to the <s>śālmalī</s> (cotton tree)? (150) Definition of <s>Paryāyokti</s> (Circumlocution):
When the matter is told not directly but described indirectly — know this as <s>Paryāyokti</s>;
accomplishing the purpose through pretext — know this as an ornament. (151) First Example:
He whose mind is the jewel of the world, whose single breath is the measure of the universe —
<s>Giridharadāsa</s> bows at the feet of all those. (152) Second Example
of <s>Paryāyokti</s>: When beautiful <s>Śyāmā</s> and <s>Śyāma</s> (<s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) both come together today,
then I shall come and attend to some task in the forest. (153)
Definition of <s>Vyājastuti</s> (Praise under Guise): <s>Vyājastuti</s> is where under the pretext of blame, praise is described;
the poet-kings describe praise under the pretext of blame, and praise under the pretext
of praise. (154) Example of <s>Vyājastuti</s> through the pretext of blame: O <s>Bhaktavatsala</s> (lover of devotees),
<s>Ghanaśyāma</s>, there is none other like you — you keep everyone's mind captivated,
whether at dusk or at dawn. (155) Example of blame under the guise of praise (<s>Vyājanindā</s>):
O <s>Yamunā</s>, you are so undiscerning — what manner is this you have adopted? With sinners
you cause the honor of your own kinsman (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) to be broken. (156) Example of praise under the guise of
blame (<s>Vyājastuti</s>): Even by taking the Name just once, millions of sins are destroyed —
blessed are those saints who continue to repeat it; such is the abode of <s>Keśava</s>. (157) Definition of
<s>Vyājanindā</s> (Blame under Guise): Where under the pretext of blame, blame itself is revealed,
the poet-kings call that <s>Vyājanindā</s>, the ornament. (158)
Example: At the gates of hell, regarding women, one remains always absorbed in passion;
submerged in the poison of sin — shame on you, O lustful one, devoid of wisdom! (159) Definition of <s>Ākṣepa</s>
(Objection): <s>Ākṣepa</s> is of three kinds — the poets describe them with discernment;
in the first, having understood what has been said, one makes a prohibition. (160) Where
prohibition merely appears to be, that is the second <s>Ākṣepa</s>; where prohibition is concealed and
a command is manifest, that is the third. (161) First Example of <s>Ākṣepa</s>: <s>Hari</s>, give up
the abode of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> and dwell in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>;
become the sovereign emperor, or else become your own servant. (162) Second Example of <s>Ākṣepa</s>: I am
not a poet, nor the glory of the earth — you are you, the world's greatness; I am not a messenger of <s>Rādhā</s> —
without you, <s>Hari</s> weeps. (163) Third Example of <s>Ākṣepa</s>:
Go, go to a foreign land, O beloved — I have no grief or fear;
my life-breath will go with you, and only this body will remain here. (164) Definition of <s>Virodhābhāsa</s> (Semblance of Contradiction):
Where contradiction appears but is not real, that is <s>Virodhābhāsa</s>;
<s>Giridharadāsa</s> says poets describe this ornament thus. (165) Example: I have no
infatuation for you, yet there is great delusion in the heart — the four eyes (two faces), O king,
both appear like lotuses. (166) Definition of <s>Vibhāvanā</s> (Causeless Effect): <s>Vibhāvanā</s> is of six
kinds — an effect without a cause; the second is when from an incomplete cause,
a full effect is produced. (167) Even when an obstruction is present,
the effect occurs — that is the third; where the effect arises from the non-cause,
that is described as the fourth. (168) When from a contrary cause the effect arises, that is the fifth;
when the cause itself is born from the effect — the sixth kind occurs. (169) First Example of
<s>Vibhāvanā</s>: Without intoxicant, <s>Hari</s>'s eyes are seen to be rolling and reddish;
without henna, her palms are red; without <s>jāvaka</s> (lac-dye), her feet are red. (170)
Second Example of <s>Vibhāvanā</s>: Seated on a single-wheeled chariot, the Sun traverses
millions of <s>kos</s> (leagues); with half-hands and feet reddened,
the charioteer (<s>Aruṇa</s>) is blameless. (171) Third Example of <s>Vibhāvanā</s>: Though absorbed in <s>Śyāma</s>'s
(<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s) heart, the mind becomes exceedingly radiant; though a king takes life,
he attains heaven, his sins destroyed. (172) Fourth Example of <s>Vibhāvanā</s>:
From coral have emerged clusters of <s>kunda</s> (jasmine) buds;
visible by daylight, the stars appear along with the moon (<s>Dvijarāja</s>). (173) Fifth Example of <s>Vibhāvanā</s>:
The breeze, cool, gentle, and fragrant, yet increases heat;
seeing the moon (<s>Uḍupati</s>) risen in bloom, the lotus becomes a house of joy. (174)
Sixth Example of <s>Vibhāvanā</s>: From the lotus emerged a river, beautiful — so says
<s>Giridharadāsa</s>; from the <s>Kalpavṛkṣa</s> (wish-fulfilling tree) emerged a treasure of gems,
accompanied by delight. (175) Definition of <s>Viśeṣokti</s> (Distinction): Where despite a sufficient cause, the effect
does not arise — poets in the world
call that <s>Viśeṣokti</s>. (176) Example: The dark cloud <s>Śyāma</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), dwelling in the heart, produces <s>rasa</s> (delight) for all every moment,
yet there is no heat there, nor any cooling

the good poet should bring to the heart that ornament,

children.text: वतत्र १७८ ॥ लंकजारि है मारि है कोटिनभटबलभौन ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Asambhava</s>. (178) The enemy of <s>Laṅkā</s> (<s>Rāma</s>) killed millions of warriors, abodes of strength;
he who destroyed the entire forest in one stride — who remained that could know? (179) Definition of <s>Asaṅgati</s>
(Incongruity): Where the impossibility of the connection between effect and cause is described,
and they are known to be mutually opposed — that is the first <s>Asaṅgati</s>. (180) Example:
The ocean-born poison-destroyer (<s>Hari</s>), beloved, destroyed the host of demons;
but the arrow of the eyes struck the eyes, causing wounds of fear. (181) Second <s>Asaṅgati</s>
Definition: When the effect of one place is attributed to another place,
the assembly of good poets should understand that as the second <s>Asaṅgati</s>. (182) Example:
On the head a crown, on the lips collyrium-like beautifying color —
today at dawn, behold, the Lord of <s>Vraja</s> has come adorned most beautifully! (183) Third <s>Asaṅgati</s> Definition:
Where one action is begun but another is accomplished —
among the three <s>Asaṅgatis</s>, that is the third. (184) Example: To remove the sorrows of the
<s>gopīs</s>, the <s>gopas</s> (cowherds) set out with crowns on their heads; but instead of removing the <s>gopīs</s>' sorrow,
they increased it further. (189) Definition of <s>Viṣama</s> (Dissimilarity): Poets describe the ornament <s>Viṣama</s>
in three ways; the conjunction of
incongruous things — know that as the first kind. (186) When the cause is of one character but the effect of another character;
the third is when one strives for the desired but obtains the undesired instead. (187)
First Example of <s>Viṣama</s>: Where are the tender sons of <s>Daśaratha</s>, and where the mighty, unyielding
bow of <s>Śiva</s>? Where the ocean, immeasurably vast leagues across, and where the tiny
squirrel (<s>Kīśa</s>)? (188) Second Example of <s>Viṣama</s>: From the flame of the lamp,
exceedingly dark smoke rises; yet from the same <s>Śyāma</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), white fame spreads across the world,
manifest. (189) Third Example of <s>Viṣama</s>: For the sake of <s>Banavārī</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>),
she went to the forest, but did not meet the moon-like <s>Gopa</s>; the women of <s>Nandagopa</s>'s household all took away
false blemishes upon themselves. (190) Definition of <s>Sama</s> (Similarity): Good poets describe <s>Sama</s> (similarity)
in three kinds; the conjunction of fitting things — know the first as
beautiful. (191) When cause and effect share one and the same aspect, that is the second;
where one strives and obtains the desired fruit, that is the third. (192) First
Example of <s>Sama</s>: Fittingly, a dot of musk adorns the forehead;
in the sweet full-moon night of autumn, the moon rises — just so. (193) Second
Example of <s>Sama</s>: The moonlight of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s words removes suffering and bestows joy;
on a night in <s>Vraja</s> with <s>Ghanaśyāma</s>, a beautiful son is born, a mine of splendor. (194)
Third Example of <s>Sama</s>: She went to <s>Vraja</s> searching for <s>Hari</s> and found <s>Giridharalāla</s>
(<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>); married for the sake of happiness, that girl gives happiness indeed. (195)
Definition of <s>Vicitra</s> (The Wonderful): Where one makes an effort contrary to the goal, yet obtains the desired fruit —
that is the ornament <s>Vicitra</s>, described by those of wise intellect. (196) Example:
Desiring happiness, the <s>yogī</s> with joy renounces happiness; to obtain wealth,
the wealthy give away their wealth upon the earth. (197) Definition of <s>Adhika</s> (The Excessive):
Where the content exceeds the container significantly —
where the content exceeds the container significantly. (198) First Example of <s>Adhika</s>:
In the boundless ocean of simile, the moon-face does not fit;
in the expanse of the narrative of knowledge, the description of <s>Nandanandana</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, son of <s>Nanda</s>) cannot be contained. (199) Second
Example of <s>Adhika</s>: How vast is the beauty of <s>Ghanaśyāma</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) — in every pore resides a universe!
How great is <s>Yaśodā</s>'s lap, where the undivided <s>Brahman</s> plays! (200) Definition of <s>Alpa</s>

children.text: लक्षण ॥ होयअल्पआधेयते और अल्प आधार ॥ गिरि
children.translated_text: (The Deficient): When the content is less than the container, or the container is less —
<s>Giridharadāsa</s> says, know that as the ornament <s>Alpa</s>. (201) Example:
An atom — smaller than the smallest — yet the beggar is famous in the world;
even that atom does not fit in the heart of the greedy one. (202) Definition of <s>Anyonya</s> (Mutual):
Where mutual benefit is described with firm determination,
the poet-folk call that the ornament <s>Anyonya</s>. (203) Example: The king is graced by the army,
and the army is graced by the king; the groom is enhanced by the wedding procession,
and the wedding procession is enhanced by the groom. (204) Definition of <s>Viśeṣa</s> (Distinction): Poets describe <s>Viśeṣa</s>
in three kinds, attending to excellence; first, where the content is described
without a well-known container. (205) Where one object is described in
many places, that is the second; where with little effort, great accomplishment is achieved, that is the third. (206)
First Example of <s>Viśeṣa</s>: The darkness departed, yet darkness remained, hidden within
the inner chamber; without a lotus, <s>Kamalālayā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>, she whose abode is the lotus) sat there, visible. (207)
Second Example of <s>Viśeṣa</s>: Sleeping or waking, in every direction and quarter, <s>Ghanaśyāma</s>
(<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) is seen; in <s>Kaṃsa</s>'s heart, at all eight watches of the day,
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> takes his rest. (208) Third Example of <s>Viśeṣa</s>: By merely reading the <s>Gītā</s>, one reads the four
<s>Vedas</s> along with their essence; by merely beholding <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, one beholds the auspicious
truth of all the worlds. (209) Definition of <s>Vyāghāta</s> (Obstruction): When from a thing, that which should arise from it
— its very opposite — arises instead from that same thing,
that is <s>Vyāghāta</s>. (210) Example: By whose remembrance, devotees attain the state of <s>Nirvāṇa</s> —
From that [ignorance], people in the world wander in delusion. ||211||
Definition of the second type of <s>Vyāghāta</s> (Obstruction): Where a purpose is obstructed by the very purpose itself, when capable [of fulfillment];
where the very cause of a purpose [becomes the obstruction] — that is the second <s>Vyāghāta</s>. ||212||
Example: Performers of action fear worldly bondage, according to scripture;
<s>Paramahaṃsas</s> (supreme renunciants) abandon action — [yet even] their fear establishes [bondage]. ||213||
Definition of <s>Kāraṇamālā</s> (Chain of Causes): Where the cause of an effect is preceded by another, and each is reversed [in order];
where there is such a chain — that is <s>Kāraṇamālā</s>. ||214|| Example:

children.text: दलते बल बलते बिजय ताते राजहुलास ॥ कृतते
children.translated_text: From an army comes strength; from strength, victory; from that, the king's delight;
from [good] deeds, a son; from a son, fair fame; from fame, a dwelling in heaven. ||215|| In reverse order:
From wealth comes virtue (<s>guṇa</s>); from virtue, study; from study, [becoming] a guru (<s>guru</s>);
from a guru, good <s>karma</s>; from good <s>karma</s>, noble action is performed. ||216|| Definition of <s>Ekāvalī</s> (Single Strand):
Where, in the manner of grasping and releasing, there is a chain of meanings —
that ornament the chief poets call <s>Ekāvalī</s>. ||217|| Example: From study
to [acquiring] virtues; from virtues to practice — know [this];
from practice to one's own knowledge; from knowledge, accept [it is] up to devotion. ||218|| Definition of <s>Mālādīpaka</s> (Garland-Illuminator):
When <s>Dīpaka</s> (Illuminator) is combined with <s>Ekāvalī</s>, it becomes <s>Mālādīpaka</s>;
thus the skilled poets describe this ornament. ||219|| Example:
In the world, from fame comes [further] fame; from fame, <s>dharma</s>; from <s>dharma</s>, beautiful <s>karma</s>;
from <s>karma</s> come the <s>Vedas</s>' words — this earth is sustained [by him]. ||220|| Definition of <s>Sāra</s> (Essence):
Where from one to another, each more excellent, there is an ornament — that is <s>Sāra</s>;
sometimes consisting of praise, sometimes of blame, sometimes of both. ||221|| Example with praise:
More worshipful than men are the gods; more than them, <s>Hari Bhagavān</s>;
more worshipful even than <s>Hari</s> are <s>Hari</s>'s devotees, in whose hearts He resides. ||222|| Example with blame:
Smaller than everything is a mustard seed; than that, a grain of dust; then an atom (<s>paramāṇu</s>);
smaller even than an atom are the virtueless — know them as such. ||223|| Example with both:
Mighty is <s>Indra</s>, then the Ten-faced (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>), then the proud <s>Bāli</s>;
mightier than <s>Bāli</s> is Greed, which laughed at the younger [brother, i.e., <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>'s] entire wealth. ||224|| Definition of <s>Yathāsaṅkhya</s> (Enumeration in Order):
Where what is stated in order is correlated in sequence;
the ornament <s>Yathāsaṅkhya</s> is excellent there, [says the poet] <s>Kavibhūṣaṇa</s>. ||225|| Example:
The god's, the enemy's, the friend's, Death's, the pauper's, the king's —
worship, kill, honor, protect, give — [each] incomparably [matched]. ||226|| Definition of <s>Paryāya</s> (Alternation):
Where, in sequence, one thing has many bases,
or many things have one [basis] — these are the two types of <s>Paryāya</s>. ||227|| First <s>Paryāya</s> example:
Childhood was in the body, then came forceful youth,
then old age arrived — now worship <s>Nandakiśora</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>). ||228|| Second <s>Paryāya</s> example:
Having abandoned my <s>Meru</s>-like mind's delusion, <s>Hari</s> made His body a dwelling;
abandoning even that, He has now settled near those [devotees]. ||229|| Definition of <s>Parivṛtti</s> (Exchange):
Where little is given and much substance is received —
that is the ornament <s>Parivṛtti</s>, described by the wise. ||230|| Example:
In the <s>Vindhya</s> mountain, with <s>Gaṅgā</s>-water and sun-flowers for worship,
giving [these] to <s>Deva</s> <s>Kapardī</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), one receives excellent gold. ||231|| Definition of <s>Parisaṅkhyā</s> (Restriction):
Where one thing is restricted to a single place,
and established as not [being] in another place — that is called <s>Parisaṅkhyā</s>. ||232|| Example:
Youthful pride cannot be found in the elderly father's home;
there is no <s>Dhanaśyāma</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) in <s>Vraja</s> — [only] in the sky does that jewel shine. ||233||
Definition of <s>Vikalpa</s> (Alternative): Where, among mutually opposed things, one [says] today;
'either this or that will happen' — that is the blameless <s>Vikalpa</s>. ||234|| Example:
Either bow your head before <s>Balarāma</s>'s plough today
or establish the city of <s>Yama</s> — [the choice is yours,] O king of the earth. ||235|| Definition of <s>Samuccaya</s> (Accumulation):
Where many actions [occur] at once for some reason —
that is the ornament the good poets bring to the heart — <s>Samuccaya</s>. ||236|| Example:
She turns her eyes, gazes at <s>Hari</s>, calls out His name;
she wanders, stands still, springs up, bends down, starts, comes to the lattice window. ||237|| Second <s>Samuccaya</s>
definition: Where each one, by one and the same cause, accomplishes one task;
that task [done by] all together — that is the second <s>Samuccaya</s>. ||238|| [Example:] <s>Gaṅgā</s>,
[<s>Bhagavad</s>-]<s>Gītā</s>, the <s>Guru</s>, the cow, <s>Gokula</s>, and the king of mountains —

children.text: गतिक्रियाअनेकको कर्त्ता एक हि होइ ॥ कविताउपकारक
children.translated_text: all these together bestow the true path and divine splendor. ||239|| Definition of <s>Kārakadīpaka</s> (Agent-Illuminator):
Where many actions in sequence have a single agent —
that is the ornament <s>Kārakadīpaka</s>, an aid to poetry. ||240|| Example:
Coming, meeting, seeing, observing — seeing [Him] in the heart, rejoicing,
playing the flute, taking His name — [He is] yours, O father of <s>Gokula</s>. ||241|| Definition of <s>Samādhi</s> (Coincidence):
Where an effect occurs from an unrelated cause, easily, by luck —
that is <s>Samādhi</s>, the cure of affliction, described by all poets. ||242|| Example:
A woman tried to skilfully stop a traveler [with] a thorn;
a cat blocked the cow's doorway — [and] the pot [she carried was] emptied of water. ||243|| Definition of <s>Pratyanīka</s> (Counter-heroism):
Where, seeing one's unconquered enemy, affliction arises on one side,
and one shows true valor — that is <s>Pratyanīka</s>. ||244|| Example:
<s>Hari</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) fought <s>Tripurāri</s> (the enemy of the three cities) with great fury;
imitating that, [<s>Kāma</s>] pierced the hearts of the best sages with arrows. ||245|| Definition of <s>Kāvyārthāpatti</s> (Poetic Implication):
When one accomplishes a great task explained to him, and a lesser one falls within [its scope] —
such an expression there is <s>Kāvyārthāpatti</s>. ||246|| Example:
Grief-stricken and disheartened <s>Mandodarī</s>, having deliberated well, [thought:]
'Mighty <s>Bāli</s> was slain — who can obstruct [<s>Rāma</s>] from killing you?' ||247|| Definition of <s>Kāvyaliṅga</s> (Poetic Reason):
Where a stated meaning is not established without justification —
justifying it with reasoning — that is <s>Kāvyaliṅga</s>. ||248|| Example:
Now there is no obstacle to crossing the ocean of worldly existence;
<s>Raghurāyajū</s> (<s>Rāma</s>) is the helper, the boat, and the helmsman. ||249|| Definition of <s>Arthāntaranyāsa</s> (Corroboration):
Where a particular is corroborated by a general [statement],
or a general by a particular — that is <s>Arthāntaranyāsa</s>. ||250|| First example:
By <s>Hari</s>'s valor, <s>Gokula</s> was saved — who can make [Him] great?
<s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> and <s>Rāvaṇa</s> were slain — who can equal <s>Yama</s>'s face? ||251|| Second example:
By the influence of the excellent <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel), [even] leaves fall into the king's hands;
by the influence of jewels, entire countries serve him. ||252|| Definition of <s>Vikasvara</s> (Blossoming):
Where a particular rests on a general, and then a particular again;
each one strengthened in sequence — that is <s>Vikasvara</s>. ||253|| Types of <s>Vikasvara</s>:
The good poets describe two types of <s>Vikasvara</s>;
the final particular is sometimes an analogy, sometimes not. ||254|| First <s>Vikasvara</s> example:
'You give truly; the virtuous give' — consider [this] like the wish-fulfilling tree;
'O sage, you have illumined my heart' — like the sun, following the way of the virtuous. ||255|| Second <s>Vikasvara</s>
example: <s>Duryodhana</s> did not heed [good counsel]; there is no remedy for the wicked;
even if one waters a neem tree with molasses, it does not become sweet. ||256||
Definition of <s>Prauḍhokti</s> (Bold Statement): Where the excellence of an accomplished thing is attributed to a [different] cause;
describing that as <s>Prauḍhokti</s>, the poets declare it to be excellent. ||257|| Example:
<s>Yamunā</s>'s waters do not bathe [His limbs]; the body of the enchanting <s>Manohar</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) is dark [by nature];
yet Her breast-hills have become hard from that — Her heart is hostile. ||258|| Definition of <s>Sambhāvanā</s> (Supposition):
'If this were, then that would be' — wherever such an expression [occurs];
that is the ornament <s>Sambhāvanā</s>, described by poets. ||259|| Example:
If I were the dust of <s>Vraja</s>, I would touch His dear feet;
if I were a bird, I would instantly go to where the Lord of <s>Vraja</s> is. ||260|| Definition of <s>Mithyādhyavasita</s> (False Attribution):
Where, to strongly establish one falsehood,
another falsehood is contrived — that is <s>Mithyādhyavasita</s>. ||261|| Example:
Building a dam across the flowing stream, making [the water] pure and cool as fire [is hot] —
O young woman! For the sake of your youthful body, renounce sensual pleasures. ||262|| Definition of <s>Lalita</s> (Graceful):
Where a present narrative is described
as if reflected in an unrelated [context] — that is called <s>Lalita</s>, silently known to the wise. ||263|| Example:
What use is repenting now? The bird has pecked the field;
you wish to cross to the other shore — without boat, without bridge. ||264|| Definition of <s>Praharṣaṇa</s> (Delight):
There are three types of <s>Praharṣaṇa</s>; the first is:
where the desired fruit is gained without any effort. ||265|| Example:
The one whom [she] desired to meet — the great, enchanting, dark one (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) —
He came of His own accord, asking 'What is your name?' ||266|| Second <s>Praharṣaṇa</s>
definition: Where a fruit greater than the desired one comes about without effort;
the poets who shower <s>rasa</s> call that the second <s>Praharṣaṇa</s>. ||267|| Example:
<s>Sudāmā</s> desired a little wealth; the Lord gave abundantly;
a wife desired just to see her beloved — [He] came and gave the gift of love. ||268||
Third <s>Praharṣaṇa</s> definition: The third is where, while applying the means to achieve a fruit,
the fruit itself comes of its own accord. ||269|| Example:
She went to the market to purchase a love-letter for news of her beloved;
on the way, she met the generous <s>Giridharalāl</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) coming from the other direction. ||270|| Definition of <s>Viṣādana</s> (Dismay):
Where whatever the mind opposes — that very thing happens;
everyone calls that the ornament <s>Viṣādana</s>. ||271|| Example:
She desired love with <s>Hari</s> — intensely, that young girl wished for it;
[but] she heard that [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] had gone to <s>Mathurā</s> city, taken by <s>Akrūra</s>. ||272||
Definition of <s>Ullāsa</s> (Effulgence): Where by the virtue or fault of one, another [is affected] —
that is the ornament <s>Ullāsa</s>, described by poets of keen intellect. ||273||
Sometimes virtue [leads to] virtue; from fault, fault; from fault, virtue;
from virtue, fault — thus the poet describes [the types]. ||274|| Virtue from virtue:
Sacred places seek to touch me; saints make [me] supremely pure;
scriptures wish me to study and bear fruit; the learned make [me] wise. ||275|| Fault from fault:
In this king's realm, birth itself is forgotten [i.e., worthless];
kings die, wealth is stolen — then what is there to weep about? ||276|| Fault from virtue:
Unlucky is that house where sacrifice and charity do not occur;
of what use is that learning for which not even a single disciple can be found? ||277|| Virtue from fault:
While admonishing, <s>Māsyā Caraṇa</s> insulted your pride;
the gain from that very fault was that <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>'s life was saved. ||278||
Definition of <s>Avajñā</s> (Contempt): Where virtue does not [lead to] virtue, and fault not to fault;
they call both types <s>Avajñā</s> — thus [speaks] the treasury of poetry. ||279||
First <s>Avajñā</s> example: Even hearing a hundred good poems, the wicked heart does not delight;
barren land yields no harvest, even when rained upon daily. ||280|| Second <s>Avajñā</s> example:
O <s>Śiva</s>, you drank the <s>hālāhala</s> (deadly poison) — what loss was there to the nectar?
lightness. 281. Definition of <s>Anujñā</s> (Permission): Where one's desire
regarding a fault [is expressed by showing] loss of virtue therein — there the ornament of <s>Anujñā</s> is described
by all the poet-kings. 282. Example: O Creator (<s>Vidhi</s>)! When will you make me
a human body — foremost in the land of <s>Vraja</s>? That I may [enjoy] being a cowherd in a cowherd's body,
completely [filled] by the power of speech. 283. Definition of <s>Leśa</s> (Trace): Where a fault is described as a virtue,

children.text: गुणहिंदोषकरियत्र ॥ कबिकुलेशबरण न करहिं लेश अलं
children.translated_text: and a virtue as a fault — the poet-clan does not describe the ornament of <s>Leśa</s>
[elsewhere]. 284. Example: Good indeed is the benevolent hunter for a beast
that is lustful — seeing others [hunted]. The deer, infatuated by the <s>rasa</s> (melody) of passion,
is forcibly killed [but it dies enraptured]. 285. Definition of <s>Mudrā</s> (Seal): When in the description of the subject-matter,
the name of another emerges — yet not in a separate context, [but] in the companionship of the text — that is <s>Mudrā</s>, abode of
virtues. 286. Example: Supreme devotee of <s>Rudra</s> conquered — intoxicated by the two feet
of [the one named] <s>Se</s>[tha]; [<s>Hari</s>]-avatāra is the proof — and the witness (<s>dohāī</s>) is yours. 287.
Definition of <s>Ratnāvalī</s> (String of Gems): Where the companion-reading is well-known, and from it another name emerges
in the description of the subject-matter — there is the abode of <s>Ratnāvalī</s>. 288.
Example: Living content in the garden, <s>Bharata</s>'s happiness is no [ordinary] joy.
Giving to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s skilled one — <s>Śatrudamana</s>-<s>Nandananda</s>. 289. Definition of <s>Tadguṇa</s>
(That-Quality): Among the mass of qualities such as form, etc., that which, abandoning its own quality,
takes the quality of another — there is <s>Tadguṇa</s>, the [ornament of] silent virtues. 290. Example:
In the woman's heart the diamond flutters — the dark color is revealed;
the golden color of the beloved's heart — both cast shadows upon each other. 291. Definition of <s>Pūrvarūpa</s>
(Prior Form): <s>Pūrvarūpa</s> is when, abandoning its own quality, something takes the quality of another,
[yet] even without the second object's connection, that state does not vanish. 292. First Example: Chanting with
a ruby garland, the ruby-named child of yours — when the gem is touched, [the hand becomes] white,
yet the palm's luster still delights [in its redness]. 293. Second Example:
What fear remained of doing [great deeds]? The fear of death — O king among men!
The long shadow of your generosity-fame remains in the world. 294. Definition of <s>Atadguṇa</s>
(Not-That-Quality): When the companion does not accept the quality such as form, etc.
of [its] principal — that ornament of <s>Atadguṇa</s> is described by the wise. 295. Example: The Dark One (<s>Śyāma</s>)
always dwells in the woman's heart; <s>Hari</s>'s rest is in the woman's heart.
Yet <s>Hari</s> does not become fair, nor does <s>Śyāmā</s> become dark. 296. Definition of <s>Anuguṇa</s>
(Conforming Quality): That quality which, being in accord with one's own quality, receives corresponding support —
therefore, and even more so, it is called by the name <s>Anuguṇa</s>. 297. Example: A cup of
decoction of <s>neem</s>-leaf juice was given to the gourd-vessel;
its bitterness cannot be expressed by those who are the skilled and wise lords. 298. Definition of <s>Milita</s> (Merged):
Where, due to similarity, in one object another object becomes hidden,
and no difference is perceived — there <s>Milita</s> is recognized. 299. Example: In the betel-
reddened [lower] lip — the friend is not [separately] seen; in the collyrium-adorned eyes,
the collyrium is not [separately] perceived. 300. Definition of <s>Sāmānya</s> (Generality): Where many objects
are similar, and no particular distinction is perceived —
they are known as all being one — there <s>Sāmānya</s> is declared. 301. Example: On the evening of the lamp-festival (<s>Dīpamālā</s>) [purchased],
the maidens are extremely beautiful. Which is the woman, which the lamp-flame? —
<s>Śyāma</s> ponders in his mind. 302. Definition of <s>Unmīlita</s> (Partially Revealed): Where due to similarity,

children.text: में अपर बस्तुजायछिपियत्र ॥ तदपि भेदकछुलखिपरै उ
children.translated_text: in one [object], another object is hidden — yet some difference is [still] perceived —
there is <s>Unmīlita</s>. 303. Example: In the bowers of green tamāla trees,
the beauty of the figures is not perceived. But by the yellow garment (<s>pītāmbara</s>), the heart recognizes
the beloved woman and her lover. 304. Definition of <s>Viśeṣa</s> (Distinction): Among objects possessing similarity,
when some distinction appears — by which one is recognized —
there <s>Viśeṣa</s> is situated. 305. Example: The white swans — all are white — how are they to be recognized?
Place milk and water before them — the entire difference is revealed. 306.
Definition of <s>Uttara</s> (Reply): Where a purposeful answer is given in hidden form —
there the ornament of <s>Uttara</s> is described by the treasury of wisdom. 307. Example: 'Enough, I shall not tell, O traveler',
[she says] — 'my home is deserted. But I shall be in the garden —
comfort in every way.' 308. Definition of <s>Citra</s> (Variegated): Where the same question
itself gives the answer, made with determination;
or where one answer [serves] many questions — that is the ornament of <s>Citra</s>. 309. Example of one question-answer: The cuckoo
sings beautifully; to <s>Kāma</s> (Love) it gives immense strength. The peacock, in the community of <s>Vraja</s>,
is the equal of the protector of the earth. 310. Many questions, one answer: 'Who moves
in the fields? Who [is in] the granary of husks? Who is the healer-herb? —
<s>Hara</s> (Śiva) is the answer, O learned ones.' 311. Definition of <s>Sūkṣma</s> (Subtle): When, perceiving another's intention, one acts with a
purposeful gesture — where the answer-form is matchless —
there is <s>Sūkṣma</s>, O poet-king. 312. Example: <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> observed <s>Raghunātha</s>'s (<s>Rāma</s>'s) direction — desiring [to know about] the night-wanderers' (demons') destruction;
placing his pointing finger on his pointing finger, drawing [the bow], <s>Rāma</s> [indicated the answer]. 313. Definition of <s>Pihita</s>
(Concealed): Where, perceiving a certain circumstance, one reveals it
through a purposeful gesture — there is the ornament of <s>Pihita</s>. 314. Example:
In the morning, seeing the beloved arrive — [the vermillion paste] applied to the forehead —
filled with anxious cleverness, the girl held up a mirror. 315. Definition of <s>Vyājoktī</s>
(Dissembled Speech): Where one conceals one's own state by speaking of another matter —
there the blessed poet-wielders describe <s>Vyājokti</s>. 316. Example: [She says:] 'O newly-
proud one! I have told you many times — [your garden has] fifty-two
rose trees — why do you not put fences around them?' 317. Definition of <s>Gūḍhokti</s> (Hidden Speech): Where someone says one thing
to one person, [but] causes another [nearby] to hear it —
so that those nearby perceive [the hidden meaning] — there is <s>Gūḍhokti</s>. 318. In the examples of <s>Gūḍhokti</s>,
two types are shown — some are rich with double meaning (<s>śleṣa</s>),
some are without <s>śleṣa</s>. 319. Example with <s>śleṣa</s> (double-meaning): [She says to the neighbor:]
'Go to the neighbor this time — if the weather (<s>bāt</s>/lover) does not come today —
the guest has come, anxious-minded — I shall stay awake (<s>surati</s>/make love) tonight.' 320. Example without <s>śleṣa</s>:
'At this moment I shall not go [to bathe] in the <s>Gaṅgā</s> — I am fearful of the bank;
therefore I shall not go to bathe, O friend — [I will stay] in the sheltered pool.' 321. Definition of <s>Vivṛtokti</s> (Open Speech): Where a secret meaning,
the poet-indicator himself reveals through a hint —
the ornament of <s>Vivṛtokti</s> is described by the treasury of wisdom. 322. The forms of <s>Vivṛtokti</s> have two methods
of hidden meaning — one occurs through the power of words (<s>śabda-śakti</s>),
and one through the power of meaning (<s>artha-śakti</s>). 323. Example of word-power: 'If you wish to take butter-milk (<s>gorasa</s>/cow-passion),
then come to my home.' — Thus speaking to the priest (who tells <s>Hari</s>), she indicated the place of love.
324. Example of meaning-power: 'My mind does not desire you — listen — [your] false, tasteless
talk.' Having thus called [him] a liar — the girl then embraced the beloved. 325. Definition of <s>Yukti</s>
(Stratagem): Where one conceals one's own secret and performs some action —
<s>Giridharadāsa</s> describes the ornament of <s>Yukti</s> there. 326.
Example: The woman, having made love with <s>Hari</s>, rose and came to that place.
Entangling her feet with the vine, she stood there sighing. 327.
Definition of <s>Lokokti</s> (Popular Saying): Where a popular proverb is deployed
within the speech at the appropriate place — that is the ornament of <s>Lokokti</s>, described by the wise, crown-jewels [of poets]. 328.
Example: 'There is said to be no grief for one dead — O sun! Teach [us this] wisdom!' —
'Listen yourself, O friend — thirst goes [only] with [drinking] water.' 329. Definition of <s>Chekokti</s> (Witty Speech):
Where the same popular saying suggests an additional meaning —
that is recognized as <s>Chekokti</s> due to the construction of [those very] words. 330. Example: The messenger
said: 'Who has been polluted by touch? There is no obstruction —
both have come together well — gold and fragrance [complement each other].' 331. Definition of <s>Vakrokti</s> (Crooked Speech): Upon hearing a statement,
driven by anger or the like, one construes a different meaning — sometimes through double-meaning (<s>śleṣa</s>),
sometimes through intonation (<s>kāku</s>) — there is <s>Vakrokti</s>. 332. Example of <s>śleṣa-vakrokti</s>:
'She who accepts (<s>mānat</s>) the union (<s>yoga</s>) of the good-minded — again and again becomes not the body.' [She replies:]
'She who accepts the yoga of the yogī — I have no love for [such].' 333. <s>Kāku-vakrokti</s>
[example]: [The friend says:] 'Abandoning you, [he went to] <s>Śyāma</s>, O friend — and another woman does not suit [him].'
Hearing 'another woman does not suit [him]' — the foolish girl raised her eyes [in anger, understanding the opposite]. 334.
Definition of <s>Svabhāvokti</s> (Natural Description): Where the nature born of childhood, etc., and the disposition
belonging to that state is described — there is <s>Svabhāvokti</s>, O poet-king.
335. Example: Toddling in the dust on the ground, setting down clumsy feet,
the darling, with broken letters, speaks delightfully to [his] friend. 336.
Definition of <s>Bhāvika</s> (Evocative): Where a past or future object is described
by the entire poet-king as present (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) — there <s>Bhāvika</s> is said [to arise]. 337.
Example of past-as-present: Playing the sweet tune on the flute, millions of [birds] singing along,
<s>Uddhava</s> says: '<s>Hari</s> still comes — driving the cows in the evening.'
338. Example of future-as-present: Among the assembly of village-lion kings, <s>Śyāmasimha</s>, the equal <s>brāhmaṇa</s> —
'I see — seizing my hand in his — [he will] quickly mount the chariot of battle.'
339. Definition of <s>Udātta</s> (Elevated): Where a praiseworthy deed of another person
[is described], or great wealth is described — that is <s>Udātta</s>, which is
of two kinds. 340. First <s>Udātta</s> example: Those whose feet are meditated upon by sages, whose sight gives delight —
they sit on the throne in the house of the hunchback woman (<s>Kubjā</s>),
shining. 341. Second <s>Udātta</s> example: Your branches bear [jewels], O woman —
bearing gems not [mere] sweepings. Those mountains are filled with [gems] — behold,
like <s>Meru</s> in appearance. 342. Definition of <s>Atyukti</s> (Exaggeration): Where the statement of generosity, valor,
separation, and the like becomes wonderfully false —
there is the ornament of <s>Atyukti</s>. 343. [Example of] generosity: 'O king, from your gifts,
there is a golden <s>Meru</s> in every house; warriors circumambulate it,
the sun makes many circuits.' 344. [Example of] valor: 'From fear of your prowess, abandoning their lives, the enemies
went to the world of <s>Yama</s> (death). Even there you do not slay them —
yet there is still dread in their hearts.' 345. [Example of] separation: 'As long as the forest-fire of separation has not arisen,
releasing its flame-sighs — until then the branches of the forest hold themselves
sheltering [from the expected conflagration].' 346. Definition of <s>Nirukti</s> (Etymology): Where, based on [a word's] derivation,
another meaning of the name is imagined — there the ornament of <s>Nirukti</s> is declared by those
who are the competent crest-jewels of the poet-clan. 347. Example: [She says:] 'Having abandoned another's [woman], you went
abroad at ease. O <s>Viṣayī</s> (sensualist), you are truthful [to your name] —
O <s>Abalā-prāṇa-harin</s> (stealer of women's lives)!' 348. Definition of <s>Pratiṣedha</s> (Prohibition): Where the report of
a well-known prohibition is shown — the ornament of <s>Pratiṣedha</s> is declared
by the most wise-minded ones. 349. Example: 'No — it is a marketplace! Here in this house,
where one does business with spears. This is a battlefield into which we have entered —
a shower of spears!' 350. Definition of <s>Vidhi</s> (Injunction): Where someone commands that which is already
established [to take place] — there the ornament of <s>Vidhi</s> is to be known — thus say
the wise. 351. Example: 'When the sun gradually reaches
the summit of the golden mountain — the life-giver would become a hundred-fold life-giver then —
Verse 352. Definition of <s>Hetu</s> (Cause): Where, along with the effect, the very cause
is described — or where the unity of both is shown — that is <s>Hetu</s>, which is of two kinds. 353
Example of the first type of <s>Hetu</s>: The clouds thundered and rose over the forest, O proud one, your pride shall be broken —
this is the task. The king drew his bow and [said]: the enemies shall be destroyed today. 354.
Example of the second type of <s>Hetu</s>: For me, the supreme state of <s>mukti</s> (liberation) — all that, O dark-complexioned <s>Ghanaśyāma</s>,
is the dust of your feet. Let all three worlds be conquered — for me, dwelling in <s>Vraja</s>-
grāma suffices. 355. Thus ends the section on <s>Arthālaṅkāra</s> (sense-ornaments). Now begins <s>Śabdālaṅkāra</s> (sound-ornaments).
Having described these hundred <s>arthālaṅkāras</s> according to his understanding,
the poet <s>Giridharadāsa</s> now describes the <s>śabdālaṅkāras</s>. 356. Definition of <s>Anuprāsa</s> (Alliteration):
Where, apart from vowels, consonants display equality —
even when combined with vowels, those same [consonants recur] — that, O poet-king, is <s>Anuprāsa</s>. 357. Example:
<s>Manamohana</s> (mind-enchanter) is splendidly beautiful; that grace I have taken into my heart. He stands firm in virtues deep,
so say his charming eyes. 358. Now, definition of <s>Chekānuprāsa</s>:
Where the equality of many consonants [occurs] in sequence, just once —
there is <s>Chekānuprāsa</s>; listen, O generous good poet. 359. Example: The splendor and beauty of the earth is great, the young maiden walks gracefully,
golden-nosed, delicate by the lake,
adorned in the forest, O blessed child. 390. Definition of <s>Vṛttyanuprāsa</s>: Where the equality of many consonants [occurs]
without sequence once, or with sequence many times —
there the ornament of <s>Vṛtti</s> is beautiful. 361. Where a single consonant
makes its equality reside — once or many times — there is <s>Vṛttyanuprāsa</s>. 362.
Example of many consonants [repeating] once: On the mountain shines the beautiful one, with fresh forest and <s>Hari</s>'s <s>rasa</s> (delight),
pure and blissful, lovely in splendor,
holding <s>Rādhikā</s>'s hand. 363. Example of consonants [repeating] in sequence many times:
The speech was made, the beloved brings joy, the moon of <s>Vraja</s>, wise among the wise. Dark-blue,
with lotus-eyes, the cuckoo calls with melodious voice. 364. Example of a single consonant
repeating once: He stands firm in deep virtues — O friend, behold my <s>Śyāma</s>
(the dark one). His image is resplendent and great, dwelling in <s>Śyāma</s>'s abode. 365.
Example of a single consonant repeating many times: Surrounding with force, the young elephant bears the heavy flood with ferocity,
turning, whirling, it attacks the mountain-flood,
with four excellent [streams]. 366. Definition of <s>Śrutyanuprāsa</s>: Consonants produced from the palate, teeth, and other
places of articulation — where there is similarity [of sound] — that is <s>Śrutyanuprāsa</s> (alliteration of similar sounds); describe it
with firm determination. 367. The clever beauty of <s>Jānakī</s> (Sītā) is lovely, her playful charm is unstained and clear,
like the moon her face [flashes] in an instant, in an instant [she] goes to the latticed window,
pure and bright. 368. Definition of <s>Antyānuprāsa</s> (end-rhyme): Where [syllables] combined with initial vowels
are enclosed by consonants — that is <s>Antyānuprāsa</s>, which is also called <s>tukānta</s>
(rhyme). 369. Example: O remover of others' suffering, with courage,
accompanied by a multitude of cowherds — where on the water's bank many parrots abound, resplendent, O mighty plowman.
370. Definition of <s>Lāṭānuprāsa</s>: Where word or meaning — of both of these —
there is manifest repetition, yet with some difference between them — there is <s>Lāṭānuprāsa</s>.
371. Example: Lotus-face, lotus-eyes — behold
the corner of [those] eyes. Be compassionate, O ocean of compassion, O thief of sorrow, [you who] steal away sorrow.
372. Definition of <s>Yamaka</s> (Paronomasia): Where groups of vowels and consonants
repeat — the poet describes that as <s>Yamaka</s>, which is of two kinds: one <s>akhaṇḍa</s> (unbroken)
and one <s>khaṇḍa</s> (broken). 373. In <s>akhaṇḍa</s>, all the meaningful words form the <s>yamaka</s>.
In <s>khaṇḍa</s>, some [repeated] words are meaningful and some are meaningless.
374. Example of <s>Akhaṇḍa Yamaka</s>: The king's ear-ornaments — [his] deeds
destroy the pride of enemies. The first letters are excellent, of excellent description, [showing] brilliant
luminous manifestation. 375. Example of <s>Khaṇḍa</s> [Yamaka]: Savior of people, lotus-bearer, of excellent bearing, treasury of beauty,
giver of the joy of refuge, conqueror of enemies' refuge,
bestower of delight in <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment). 376. Thus, both the ornaments of sound and meaning
have been completed in this manner. Reading these, the virtuous ones who appreciate qualities
shall attain supreme happiness. 377. The poet [says]: This <s>Bhāratī-bhūṣaṇa</s> (Ornament of Speech) is the supreme ornament of <s>Bhāratī</s> (Sarasvatī).
Cherishing devotion at the feet of <s>Bhāratī</s>, may the good poets read and master
this work. 378. By various means the virtuous [praise] <s>Śiva</s>, and <s>Śiva</s> [praises] the virtuous, performing [worship] with the dust of [divine] feet —
again and again, <s>Giridharadāsa</s> bows at their feet. 379.
Thus ends the <s>Bhāratī-bhūṣaṇa</s>, the treatise on <s>alaṅkāra</s> (literary ornaments), composed by the lord among poets, <s>Bābū Giridharadāsa</s>,
a bee at the lotus-feet of <s>Śrī Nandanandana</s> (Kṛṣṇa, son of Nanda), lord of wealth.
